## Open

### F-334 — A passing Storybook run rewrites 22 committed markup snapshots

> _2026-10-01 · tools/blong-log · open_

Running `npm run storybook:test:ci` in tools/blong-log leaves the working tree dirty: the runner
writes src/client/__markup_snapshots__/*.json on every run from .storybook/test-runner.cjs, which is
an analysis artifact and not a jest comparison, so what it writes depends on the browser it ran
with. Chromium 1243 serializes a computed style as `overflow: clip` where the committed file says
`visible`, so one run produced 22 modified files that a commit would have to explain and that no
assertion depends on. The 21 image snapshots in __image_snapshots__ are the comparison that matters;
those passed. Worth either listing the markup snapshots in .gitignore or normalising the style
properties they carry, so a local run does not hand the author a diff they did not ask for.

### F-531 — The CI storybook leg served a dev server whose output went into the log

> _2026-10-15 · tools/blong-log · open_

`tools/blong-log` was the only package whose `ci-test` ran a Storybook dev server: the chain
`blong-dev test || …; node --run storybook:test:ci` started `storybook dev`, so the CI log carried
the server's banner and its Vite build chatter next to the test results — the "not aligned with the
rest" the package's own skill already describes the other way round ("build static → serve → test →
exit"). `core/blong-browser` has the same script but never calls it from `ci-test`, which is why it
never showed.

The script now runs `storybook dev --ci --quiet --loglevel warn` with its output redirected to a
temp file, and prints that file only when the test runner fails — the log carries the tests'
results, and the server's output is still there for the failure that needs it. Verified by running
the script: 22 story tests pass and no banner or Vite line reaches the log.

Fixing the server left the larger half: the runner's own report — a `PASS` line, every story with
its `✓ smoke-test`, and jest's summary — was most of the log. It now goes to
`.ci-report/storybook.log`, which the workflow already uploads with `tools/*/.ci-report`; the script
prints one summary line and that path, and dumps the file when the runner fails, which is the shape
the tap leg already has. The runner also needs `FORCE_COLOR=0 NO_COLOR=1`: jest colours the
`Test Suites:` label, so an anchored grep matched nothing and the first attempt printed an empty
summary line. Verified end to end: two lines for the storybook leg, 22 tests and 21 snapshots
passing, tap 82 pass.

### F-541 — The storybook runner takes fewer options than it lists

> _2026-10-16 · tools/blong-log · open_

The runner validates its options against an allow-list, so the options jest itself would accept are
rejected with the runner's help text and a pointer to its issue tracker: `--reporters jest-junit`
and the equals form `--outputFile=<path>` both died that way, while `--json --outputFile <path>`
(the space form) is accepted and writes exactly the file a report bridge can read. The hooks are
narrower than they look too: the context `postVisit` is handed carries only `id`, `title`, `name`
and `hasFailure` — no story parameters — so a story cannot declare how long it needs before it is at
rest, and the runner keeps that list itself (`SETTLE_MS` in `.storybook/test-runner.cjs`). That wait
is what makes the shot a property of the rendering rather than of the machine: a story still
streaming rows when the shot is taken is compared against however many rows the runner delivered.
Probing an option costs a full storybook run, so try the space form of a jest option before
concluding the runner does not support it.

## Resolved

### F-773 — The log viewer could not be started or opened, and no test noticed

> _2026-11-20 · tools/blong-log · resolved_

Reviewing `tools/blong-log` against lukaot turned up three defects that no test covered, because
each one is outside what the package tests: its producer was a pino transport and the framework had
stopped writing through pino, so the server had nothing feeding it; `public/index.html` did not
exist in any environment, so `/` answered 404 and the UI could not be opened at all; and its local
imports used `.js` specifiers that only the tap loader resolves, so the documented `npx blong-log`
could not start.

None of the three failed a test, and none would fail one now unless a test opened the page or
started the CLI. That is the lesson: a tool with a rendered surface needs one test that starts it
the way a person does and asks for what a person asks for — the page, and an entry in it. The e2e
test written with this change does the second half (a lukaot writer feeding the server, read back
through the API); the first is the remaining gap and is recorded as a todo.

Closed: producer moved to a lukaot writer with an e2e test, index.html added, .ts/.tsx specifiers,
request-derived addresses; the CLI smoke test is T-742.

### F-774 — An expanded grid row was measured, so it flickered and clipped its own detail

> _2026-11-20 · tools/blong-log · resolved_

The grid has to be told a row's height as data, not as a function: `rowHeight` on the column config
is one number for every row, and a function is silently ignored, which is why the expanded rows were
drawn at the theme's default and the detail was clipped. `rowHeight` on the row object is read, and
`_rowHeightFromData` makes the virtual scroller add up the same per-row heights — without it the
scroll range is computed from the default and an expanded row near the end cannot be reached.

`autoRowHeight` measures the rendered cell instead. That is what made an expanded row scrolled out
of view come back collapsed for a frame: it is drawn at its closed height, then it jumps when the
measurement lands, so the scroller repositions itself and a scroll gesture over that row can stop
working. The height is therefore derived from the record alone — bytes for a frame, lines for a
document — and never measured; the detail scrolls inside its own viewport instead.

Three more things this cost, all visible rather than diagnosed. A cell has to be the line plus the
padding or its text is cut in half: the theme pads a cell by 8px and sets a 20px line height, so the
28px row that looked dense was clipping every column, and the fix is a 16px line, 4px padding and a
26px row. `white-space: pre-wrap` on an expanded cell renders the newlines and indents between the
JSX elements as lines, which is the band of blank space that appeared above the first panel — it
belongs on the text that needs it. And the message and the JSON expand separately: one set of
expanded ids meant opening a record's JSON also opened its sentence.

Keyboard: space toggles the detail of the column the focused cell belongs to, read from the cell's
`data-col-id` (written with a leading colon, as `data-row-id` is) rather than from the grid's state,
which reports cells and rows under keys this version does not document.
